title: Death Stranding Director's Cut
provenance: Reported by zezzzz11 (highball#514, 2026-10-26), Apple M4 Max, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.22, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r29, D3DMetal: stopped with 'requires a CPU with AVX support' until AVX was advertised in the environment's settings, then worked fine. The original Death Stranding's page and recipe carried the fix, but the Director's Cut is its own Steam app, so it never reached this copy. Not verified by the maintainer. Arpitt-101 (highball-db#1024, 2026-11-06), Apple M5, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.23, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, D3DMetal, rated 4 of 5 after 33 minutes: with the game's recipe, nothing stated about what wasn't perfect. hsuanice (highball-db#1374, 2026-11-21), Apple M1 Ultra, macOS 27.2.1, Highball 0.10.28, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r31, D3DMetal, rated 4 of 5 after 371 minutes: with the game's recipe, the Metal HUD on and the steam, vcrun2022, xact and controller-sdl recipes. The menu screens flicker slightly while the game itself is fine, and frame pacing is uneven even at 60 fps, with the Metal HUD showing Composited presentation. On a 10 channel Universal Audio Thunderbolt interface the sound is pulled to the left, and starting the game with a two channel output such as the Mac's speakers, then switching back to the interface once it runs, fixes that. A DualSense needs the Controllers through SDL recipe: without it the game finds the DualSense on its own, with buttons mismapped and the camera spinning, and with it the prompts are right once Options, Controller, Change button icons is set to PlayStation. The player tried the Wine 11 engine x64-crossover26.3-r32 (D3DMetal 4.0b3) and saw a lower frame rate there, and says they went back to x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r30, while the report's engine is r31. hsuanice (highball-db#1411, 2026-11-23), Apple M1 Ultra, macOS 27.2.1, Highball 0.10.28, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r31, D3DMetal, rated 5 of 5 after 153 minutes: with the game's recipe and the steam, vcrun2022, xact and controller-sdl recipes.
notes: DirectX 12, so D3DMetal. Like the original, the game refuses to start without AVX, which Rosetta hides unless asked, so the recipe advertises it to the game. Works once that is on, by the reporter's account on an M4 Max. Nothing was measured here. A report on an M5 rates it playable over 33 minutes with D3DMetal and the recipe on the default engine (r28) (highball-db#1024). An M1 Ultra rated it playable over 371 minutes with D3DMetal and the recipe on the Wine 10 engine r31 (the D3DMetal 4 line), with slight flicker on menu screens and uneven frame pacing at 60 fps. On a 10 channel audio interface the sound was pulled to the left unless the game started on a two channel output, and a DualSense plays right through the Controllers through SDL recipe. The Wine 11 engine r32 with D3DMetal 4.0b3 gave a lower frame rate for that player (highball-db#1374).

knownIssues.symptom: "Death Stranding requires a CPU with AVX support" at launch
knownIssues.fix: the recipe advertises AVX (from the next Highball version). By hand now, turn on Advertise AVX in the environment's settings

knownIssues.symptom: The sound is pulled to the left on a 10 channel audio interface, a Universal Audio Thunderbolt one (M1 Ultra, Wine 10 r31, highball-db#1374)
knownIssues.fix: start the game with a two channel output selected, such as the Mac's speakers, then switch back to the interface once the game runs, per the player

knownIssues.symptom: Without the Controllers through SDL recipe the game finds a DualSense on its own, with buttons mismapped and the camera spinning (M1 Ultra, highball-db#1374)
knownIssues.fix: keep the Controllers through SDL recipe on the environment, and set Options, Controller, Change button icons to PlayStation for the right prompts, per the player

knownIssues.symptom: Menu screens flicker slightly while the game itself is fine, and frame pacing is uneven even at 60 fps, with the Metal HUD showing Composited presentation (M1 Ultra, Wine 10 r31, D3DMetal, highball-db#1374)
